Subject: Pacing & concurrency playbook — post-call recap and concrete next steps

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. I’ve attached a lightweight sizing worksheet (CSV) and a short notes PDF from Diego with the initial math.

Call highlights (what we heard)
- Primary flow: interactive product recommendations in checkout (real-time suggestions).
- SLO ask: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 250ms for interactive flows.
- Typical session: 1–3 inference calls per customer interaction; average request size today ~380 tokens (pre/post-processing combined).
- Traffic shape: baseline 4–6 QPS, short crest windows up to ~28 QPS for 30–90s during marketing bursts.
- Streaming: you’d like partial token streaming for suggestions (chunked every ~120 tokens) to show quick hits.

Initial sizing questions we need from you (short list)
1) Can you upload a 5–10 minute sample of production ingress (timestamps + tokens/request or bytes/request)? A log snippet is fine.
2) What percent of traffic must be streaming vs full-response (estimate)?
3) Expected growth window for the pilot (1 month / 3 months / other)?

Our early interpretation (high level)
- If the crest windows are ~28 QPS with avg 380 tokens, that’s ~10,640 tokens/sec at peak. Sustained baseline at 5 QPS => ~1,900 tokens/sec.
- For streaming: we’ll treat each chunk as smaller calls (120-token chunks) which changes effective QPS of the serving layer; we’ll show two options in the worksheet (dedicated instances vs shared-hosted with autoscale).

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- Today: I’ll upload the sizing worksheet (attached) and a short note from Diego explaining the assumptions.
- You: drop a 5–10 minute request sample (prod or staging) to the Drive link or reply with the log attached.
- Tue 10/06: 30-min follow-up to validate numbers and agree on pilot SLA (I’ll propose 10:00 PT).

If any of the numbered bullet assumptions above are off, flag them in reply.

Thanks —
Sergio

Sergio — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and a quick log sample attached (prod_sample_rps.log).

Clarifications from our side:
- The 28 QPS crest is accurate for promotional blasts but usually lasts 45–75s; happens ~2x/day currently.
- Avg tokens/request: we measured 370–420 tokens; 380 is a good working average.
- Streaming split: roughly 60% of requests should be streaming-enabled (fast UX path), 40% can be full-response.
- Latency expectation: 250ms p95 is our goal; for the streaming path, we expect first-chunk <120ms.

Extra context:
- We can provide 10 minutes of high-fidelity logs this week; will upload to the Drive link you shared.
- Pilot timeline: we prefer a 30-day pilot with an optional 3-month expansion.

Two quick asks for your team:
1) Can you outline a fallback plan if streaming partials miss the first-chunk target? (We’d want graceful degrade to full-response rather than erroring.)
2) Confirm whether Redwood prefers to size by tokens/sec or target QPS for pilot procurement.

Thanks —
Priya Rao

Quick technical notes and a conservative first-pass sizing to share with Priya (I attached the small PDF). I ran the rough math off the numbers from the call + Priya’s log sample.

Assumptions used (conservative)
- Avg tokens/request: 380 tokens
- Streaming split: 60% streaming (120-token chunks), 40% full-response
- Peak crest: 28 QPS sustained over 60s
- Baseline: 5 QPS steady-state

Converted metrics
- Peak tokens/sec (full-equivalent):
  - If all requests were full: 28 QPS * 380 tokens = 10,640 tokens/sec.
  - With 60% streaming (we treat a streaming request as ~3 chunks of 120 tokens => ~3 calls per logical request) effective call QPS increases, but per-call tokens are lower. For capacity we convert back to tokens/sec: streaming portion = 0.6 * 28 * 380 = 6,374 tokens/sec; non-streaming portion = 0.4 * 28 * 380 = 4,256 tokens/sec; total ~10,630 tokens/sec (same token budget, different concurrency profile).
- Baseline tokens/sec: 5 QPS * 380 = 1,900 tokens/sec.

Sizing heuristic (ballpark)
- Using our serving profiles, a single midsize GPU node (Redwood profile: gen-highmem-1) can sustain ~18k tokens/sec for batch-optimized non-streaming workloads at modest latency SLOs. Streaming lowers efficiency because of more incremental calls; for the mixed profile above we recommend reserving a single GPU for the pilot crest buffer and autoscaling to a second GPU if crest > 18k tokens/sec or if per-request latency degrades.

Operational notes / mitigation
- Autoscale thresholds: scale-up at sustained tokens/sec > 12k for 30s; scale-down after 120s below 6k.
- Fallback for missed streaming first-chunk: return the last-best partial and kick a low-latency full-response on a best-effort background thread; that keeps UX responsive but avoids full error bubbling. We can propose a canary where 10% of streaming requests fall back to that path to validate behavior.

Deliverables I’ll prepare for Tue’s call
- A filled sizing worksheet with the two options (dedicated pilot capacity vs hosted-autoscale) with estimated costs.
- Short runbook for streaming fallback and observability signals (first-chunk latency, chunk-drop rate, queue length).

LMK if you want me to include estimated tail-latency numbers for p99/p999; I can model those but need more sample variance from your logs.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Fallback behavior: agreed — first-chunk fallback to best-partial + background full-response is what we’ll prototype. Diego will include the runbook.
